compare_blocks.body:
Align three conditions before reading: the same version of the definition, the same batch of source documents, the same reporting deadline. Those conditions are what makes the two columns comparable; if one produces the numbers and the other only reviews, duty will cover both columns.

The six rows come from the same definition, the same data and the same signatory; the right-hand column states which axis the row sits on. The same person would switch columns under different conditions, so read the conditions before the tendency.

| The same event (one definition, one batch of documents, one deadline) | ENTJ: an example starting from execution conditions | INTP: an example starting from definitional consistency | Where this row's basis sits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In the same meeting room these two look alike: both will argue about the definition of one metric until the room empties, and neither accepts "that is how we have always calculated it" as a reason. The resemblance comes from the shared N and T — both look at pattern and possibility when sourcing, and both want a standard that can be applied consistently.

The difference is not who is more rigorous, but where the rigour points. ENTJ more often puts attention on whether the rule can be executed: who signs, which day it takes effect, who rechecks it. INTP more often puts attention on whether the rule can be recomputed: at which step the two accounts diverge, whether the edge cases are internally consistent.

### When the definition does not line up, two necessary pieces of work

A blocked definition usually lacks two things: an executable arrangement, and a recomputable definition. ENTJ more often sees the first as the gap — who decides this, which day the change takes effect, when the old version stops being used; INTP more often sees the second as the gap — at which step the two calculations diverge, which keyword means different things in two places. The first turns a disagreement into responsibility and dates; the second turns it into a proposition that can be tested.

This has nothing to do with who speaks first or who moves first. In the same meeting, ENTJ may spend the whole hour on definitions, and INTP may be pushed into fixing an effective date; the difference is which gap each more often treats as the one that must be closed first.

Each approach leaves a blind spot. Someone who only closes the arrangement may weld a wrong definition into the process, and changing it next time means going through approval again; someone who only closes the definition may check it thoroughly while nobody publishes a new version. The cost is not about preference but about who has the authority and who is waiting for this number.

Keep the counterexamples too: when INTP is made the owner of the definition, they may also lay out the signing order; when ENTJ meets a rule they cannot make sense of, they may also turn the meeting into a definition seminar. A position describes emphasis inside the model, not a fixed sequence of actions.

### Why the categories match and the attitudes reverse

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe. The category order is identical — Thinking, Intuition, Sensing, Feeling from first to fourth — and what changes is the attitude marked at each position: Te against Ti, Ni against Ne, Se against Si, Fi against Fe.

The derivation starts with the first two positions. E/I decides whether the dominant turns outward or inward, and J/P decides whether the outward step is judging or perceiving. ENTJ leans E and J: the dominant is an outward judging function, extraverted Thinking, Te; the auxiliary must be an inward perceiving function, taking Intuition, so introverted Intuition, Ni. INTP leans I and P: the dominant is inward, introverted Thinking, Ti; the outward step is perceiving, so the auxiliary is extraverted Intuition, Ne. The third and fourth positions are filled by the remaining two categories, Se and Fi, and Si and Fe.

Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not consistent across tables: some give only the function name, some label differently. This page uses the common writing and does not attribute that labelling to the Foundation as its only convention. Positions describe emphasis in preference and are not used to predict behavioural order, whether a collaboration goes smoothly, or mutual attraction. The four preferences are explained one by one in the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp).
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Joining the same data team, the handover usually splits into two artefacts: a definition sheet that states the signature and effective date, and a validation note that can be recomputed. Who writes which is decided by authority and familiarity, not by type.

### The quarterly management report: value shipped or value confirmed as delivered

(Fictional scene.) Three days before close, the sales team counts the value of orders shipped, the analysis team counts the value of orders confirmed as delivered, and the two internal totals differ substantially. This concerns the extraction basis of internal management reports only, not accounting revenue recognition; the external accounting basis is determined by finance under the applicable policy and contract terms, and this page compares extraction and review only, offering no accounting treatment advice.

One trade-off is about how this definition lands: bring the three parties together, agree a temporary method for the quarter, put it in writing by email, name an effective date, note when the old version stops, and turn the difference into a reconciliation sheet with an owner on every line.

The other trade-off is about whether the definition is consistent: go through the extraction conditions of both reports, find that the difference concentrates in the batch shipped across the month end, and that "signed" corresponds to two timestamps in the system, either of which can be justified.

The same analyst can do both kinds of check, and each trade-off has a cost. Someone watching only implementation may treat this quarter's temporary method as the conclusion and cover up the two-timestamp problem; someone watching only consistency may check thoroughly and miss the reporting window.

The check: each writes three lines — which field was used this time, which documents were affected, and where the problem should be stopped next time — then they swap and compare line by line. This is organising information, not scoring anyone.

### Explaining a definition change to the business: how to write the email

(Fictional scene.) The business lead will not accept the change, because the bonus is tied to the old number. One approach calculates the scope of impact and offers a transition period and a remedy; the other points out which orders the old definition necessarily gets wrong, with two specific order numbers attached. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

The sticking point is not the argument but the basis: an email with only a plan reads as pressure, and one with only flaws reads as evasion. Split it into two sections — what changes and when it takes effect, and why it cannot stay — and with both present the reader knows what to do.

Two counterexamples: ENTJ may leave the conclusion out for now so the other person can step back without losing face; INTP may accept a definition they are not happy with in order to hit the reporting deadline. Both show the same person changing basis under different conditions, and a single piece of writing is not a criterion.

### A fingerprint lock for the parents' flat

(Fictional scene.) Your parents keep misplacing their keys and have a fixed budget for a fingerprint lock. One approach weighs price, availability and support. Another checks the door thickness, the existing holes and whether there is a way to unlock the door during a power outage. Either person could do both. This fictional example illustrates buying criteria and cannot identify someone’s type.

Each focus has its own failure mode: buying on budget and schedule may end with a door that is the wrong thickness; checking only specifications may take so long that the parents are still dealing with misplaced keys. Both are guarding against the same thing — buying wrong and returning — one with time and budget, the other with a specification sheet.

Keep the counterexamples: INTP may also order immediately when the parents push; ENTJ may also have someone measure the door before ordering. Who pays, who lives nearby and who arranges the installation all change where the attention lands.

The parents will not care which line of thinking is cleverer; they will ask which day it can be fitted. The check: before ordering, each writes three conditions that would force a return — door thickness, hole spacing, unlocking when the power is out — and only pay when all three match, asking the seller first if one does not.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
The first slip is treating volume in a meeting as evidence of type. ENTJ will also listen through a round before speaking on an unfamiliar topic; INTP can also go into great detail on a field they have checked themselves. How much someone speaks depends on familiarity with the topic, how the meeting is chaired and where they sit, and cannot be read backwards into a type.

The second is treating rigour as the common trait of Thinking types. Both lean T, and T is not the differing item in this pair; the fork is E/I and J/P — whether attention goes outward or inward more often, and whether the outward step forms an arrangement or keeps options. Whether closure happens in the meeting or afterwards depends on the chair, the agenda and who has authority, and is not a type clue.

The third is treating the last signatory as the more senior. Signing is a role the process assigns; ENTJ only offers comments on modules someone else owns, and INTP signs when made responsible. Material that only records "who decided" distinguishes jobs.

The fourth is treating "who moves first" as the criterion. On the same definition, whether responsibility or the definition gets dismantled first depends heavily on deadlines, authority and information held; recording the order as type evidence collapses the moment someone changes role or project.

body: Joining the same data team, the handover usually splits into two artefacts: a definition sheet that states the signature and effective date, and a validation note that can be recomputed. Who writes which is decided by authority and familiarity, not by type.

(Fictional scene.) Three days before close, the sales team counts the value of orders shipped, the analysis team counts the value of orders confirmed as delivered, and the two internal totals differ substantially. One trade-off is about how this definition lands: bring the three parties together, agree a temporary method for the quarter, put it in writing by email, name an effective date, note when the old version stops, and turn the difference into a reconciliation sheet with an owner on every line.

The other trade-off is about whether the definition is consistent: go through the extraction conditions of both reports, find that the difference concentrates in the batch shipped across the month end, and that "signed" corresponds to two timestamps in the system, either of which can be justified.

The same analyst can do both kinds of check, and each trade-off has a cost. Someone watching only implementation may treat this quarter's temporary method as the conclusion and cover up the two-timestamp problem; someone watching only consistency may check thoroughly and miss the reporting window.

(Fictional scene.) The business lead will not accept the change, because the bonus is tied to the old number. sections.title: Quick answer

body: In the same meeting room these two look alike: both will argue about the definition of one metric until the room empties, and neither accepts "that is how we have always calculated it" as a reason. The resemblance comes from the shared N and T — both look at pattern and possibility when sourcing, and both want a standard that can be applied consistently.

The difference is not who is more rigorous, but where the rigour points. ENTJ more often puts attention on whether the rule can be executed: who signs, which day it takes effect, who rechecks it. INTP more often puts attention on whether the rule can be recomputed: at which step the two accounts diverge, whether the edge cases are internally consistent.
### When the definition does not line up, two necessary pieces of work

A blocked definition usually lacks two things: an executable arrangement, and a recomputable definition. ENTJ more often sees the first as the gap — who decides this, which day the change takes effect, when the old version stops being used; INTP more often sees the second as the gap — at which step the two calculations diverge, which keyword means different things in two places. The first turns a disagreement into responsibility and dates; the second turns it into a proposition that can be tested.

This has nothing to do with who speaks first or who moves first. In the same meeting, ENTJ may spend the whole hour on definitions, and INTP may be pushed into fixing an effective date; the difference is which gap each more often treats as the one that must be closed first.

Each approach leaves a blind spot. Someone who only closes the arrangement may weld a wrong definition into the process, and changing it next time means going through approval again; someone who only closes the definition may check it thoroughly while nobody publishes a new version. The cost is not about preference but about who has the authority and who is waiting for this number.

Keep the counterexamples too: when INTP is made the owner of the definition, they may also lay out the signing order; when ENTJ meets a rule they cannot make sense of, they may also turn the meeting into a definition seminar. A position describes emphasis inside the model, not a fixed sequence of actions.
### Why the categories match and the attitudes reverse

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe. The category order is identical — Thinking, Intuition, Sensing, Feeling from first to fourth — and what changes is the attitude marked at each position: Te against Ti, Ni against Ne, Se against Si, Fi against Fe.

The derivation starts with the first two positions. E/I decides whether the dominant turns outward or inward, and J/P decides whether the outward step is judging or perceiving. ENTJ leans E and J: the dominant is an outward judging function, extraverted Thinking, Te; the auxiliary must be an inward perceiving function, taking Intuition, so introverted Intuition, Ni. INTP leans I and P: the dominant is inward, introverted Thinking, Ti; the outward step is perceiving, so the auxiliary is extraverted Intuition, Ne. The third and fourth positions are filled by the remaining two categories, Se and Fi, and Si and Fe.

Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not consistent across tables: some give only the function name, some label differently. This page uses the common writing and does not attribute that labelling to the Foundation as its only convention. Positions describe emphasis in preference and are not used to predict behavioural order, whether a collaboration goes smoothly, or mutual attraction. The four preferences are explained one by one in the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp).

body: Align three conditions before reading: the same version of the definition, the same batch of source documents, the same reporting deadline. Those conditions are what makes the two columns comparable; if one produces the numbers and the other only reviews, duty will cover both columns.

The six rows come from the same definition, the same data and the same signatory; the right-hand column states which axis the row sits on. The same person would switch columns under different conditions, so read the conditions before the tendency.

| The same event (one definition, one batch of documents, one deadline) | ENTJ: an example starting from execution conditions | INTP: an example starting from definitional consistency | Where this row's basis sits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A definition note arrives; can it be used as it stands | May prefer to agree on a provisional implementation plan under the same approval requirements | May prefer to keep several implementation options open while reviewing the same draft | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| The departments' figures differ substantially | Look for a pattern across affected reports that could explain the gap | Look for a shared assumption that could explain where the calculations diverge | Looking for patterns and possible explanations, the shared N |
| Someone wants an exception for one client | Would the same exception criteria apply consistently to other clients in the same circumstances? | Does the proposed exception contradict the rule, and can it be stated consistently? | Basis for judgement, the shared T |
| The report structure needs a new version | May agree on provisional release and retirement dates within the same constraints | May keep multiple transition plans open while the same dependencies are clarified | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Asked to produce a number today | Produce it on the current definition, and list the gaps as actions with names attached | Add an intermediate table that can be recomputed, and mark which rows are not yet usable | Delivery conventions and recomputable evidence; both check |
| Quarterly review | Whether every milestone was assessed against the same criteria | Whether each conclusion follows from the evidence and the same set of assumptions | Basis for judgement, the shared T |

The differences in the table are not a scale of ability. An INTP with years of cost accounting more often starts from signatures and effective dates, and an ENTJ taking over definition management for the first time may spend two days reading the field notes. body: Joining the same data team, the handover usually splits into two artefacts: a definition sheet that states the signature and effective date, and a validation note that can be recomputed. Who writes which is decided by authority and familiarity, not by type.
### The quarterly management report: value shipped or value confirmed as delivered

(Fictional scene.) Three days before close, the sales team counts the value of orders shipped, the analysis team counts the value of orders confirmed as delivered, and the two internal totals differ substantially. This concerns the extraction basis of internal management reports only, not accounting revenue recognition; the external accounting basis is determined by finance under the applicable policy and contract terms, and this page compares extraction and review only, offering no accounting treatment advice.

One trade-off is about how this definition lands: bring the three parties together, agree a temporary method for the quarter, put it in writing by email, name an effective date, note when the old version stops, and turn the difference into a reconciliation sheet with an owner on every line.

The other trade-off is about whether the definition is consistent: go through the extraction conditions of both reports, find that the difference concentrates in the batch shipped across the month end, and that "signed" corresponds to two timestamps in the system, either of which can be justified.

The same analyst can do both kinds of check, and each trade-off has a cost. Someone watching only implementation may treat this quarter's temporary method as the conclusion and cover up the two-timestamp problem; someone watching only consistency may check thoroughly and miss the reporting window.

The check: each writes three lines — which field was used this time, which documents were affected, and where the problem should be stopped next time — then they swap and compare line by line. This is organising information, not scoring anyone.
### Explaining a definition change to the business: how to write the email

(Fictional scene.) The business lead will not accept the change, because the bonus is tied to the old number. One approach calculates the scope of impact and offers a transition period and a remedy; the other points out which orders the old definition necessarily gets wrong, with two specific order numbers attached. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

The sticking point is not the argument but the basis: an email with only a plan reads as pressure, and one with only flaws reads as evasion. Split it into two sections — what changes and when it takes effect, and why it cannot stay — and with both present the reader knows what to do.

Two counterexamples: ENTJ may leave the conclusion out for now so the other person can step back without losing face; INTP may accept a definition they are not happy with in order to hit the reporting deadline. Both show the same person changing basis under different conditions, and a single piece of writing is not a criterion.
### A fingerprint lock for the parents' flat

(Fictional scene.) Your parents keep misplacing their keys and have a fixed budget for a fingerprint lock. One approach weighs price, availability and support. Another checks the door thickness, the existing holes and whether there is a way to unlock the door during a power outage. Either person could do both. This fictional example illustrates buying criteria and cannot identify someone’s type.

Each focus has its own failure mode: buying on budget and schedule may end with a door that is the wrong thickness; checking only specifications may take so long that the parents are still dealing with misplaced keys. Both are guarding against the same thing — buying wrong and returning — one with time and budget, the other with a specification sheet.

Keep the counterexamples: INTP may also order immediately when the parents push; ENTJ may also have someone measure the door before ordering. Who pays, who lives nearby and who arranges the installation all change where the attention lands.

The parents will not care which line of thinking is cleverer; they will ask which day it can be fitted. The check: before ordering, each writes three conditions that would force a return — door thickness, hole spacing, unlocking when the power is out — and only pay when all three match, asking the seller first if one does not.

body: The first slip is treating volume in a meeting as evidence of type. ENTJ will also listen through a round before speaking on an unfamiliar topic; INTP can also go into great detail on a field they have checked themselves. How much someone speaks depends on familiarity with the topic, how the meeting is chaired and where they sit, and cannot be read backwards into a type.

The second is treating rigour as the common trait of Thinking types. Both lean T, and T is not the differing item in this pair; the fork is E/I and J/P — whether attention goes outward or inward more often, and whether the outward step forms an arrangement or keeps options. Whether closure happens in the meeting or afterwards depends on the chair, the agenda and who has authority, and is not a type clue.

The third is treating the last signatory as the more senior. Signing is a role the process assigns; ENTJ only offers comments on modules someone else owns, and INTP signs when made responsible. Material that only records "who decided" distinguishes jobs.

The fourth is treating "who moves first" as the criterion. On the same definition, whether responsibility or the definition gets dismantled first depends heavily on deadlines, authority and information held; recording the order as type evidence collapses the moment someone changes role or project.

body: When two results differ, check the item bank first: the same questionnaire, language version, time window and scoring convention. Then look at the answering situation — if you were mainly thinking about the demands of your job, the answers may reflect a role rather than an everyday preference, and you cannot infer from that which way the score would move.

An exercise you can run yourself: take one fictional definition note and write two sets of conditions. First: a clear signatory exists but the field definitions are undecided — what is still needed. Second: the field definitions are settled but nobody has the authority to publish — what is still needed. In each, write down how authority, deadline and missing information change your choice.

These notes are for understanding trade-offs; they are not scored, do not assign a type, and set no minimum number. Counterexamples matter as much: using the other kind of basis on the same sort of matter shows both approaches are within your range.

sections.body_md:
ENTJ and INTP share N and T, and differ on E/I and J/P.

- N (Intuition, shared): gathering information, both more often take connections, patterns and possibility first, rather than checking observable facts and past experience one by one.
- T (Thinking, shared): judging, both more often weigh impersonal criteria that can be applied consistently, rather than asking first what the matter means for the people involved.
- E/I: ENTJ leans E, with attention and energy turning outward more often, onto people, meetings and things that can be delivered; INTP leans I and more often works the model out internally first. This describes direction, not talkativeness and not social skill.
- J/P: facing the outer world, ENTJ leans J and more often forms arrangements and conclusions first; INTP leans P and more often keeps options and keeps collecting information. This describes outward stance, not speed of execution.

Using the type-dynamics convention on this page, the stacks are: Te–Ni–Se–Fi for ENTJ and Ti–Ne–Si–Fe for INTP. The category order is identical and the attitude marked at every position reverses; the attitude of the third process is written differently elsewhere, and this labelling is a convention adopted here, not the Foundation's only version.

The report case compares two kinds of work that are both necessary: making a rule executable, and making a definition recomputable. Either person can do both. Responsibilities, deadlines and access to information can shape what happens first, so the order offers no basis for assigning a type.
sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
In the same meeting room these two look alike: both will argue about the definition of one metric until the room empties, and neither accepts "that is how we have always calculated it" as a reason. The resemblance comes from the shared N and T — both look at pattern and possibility when sourcing, and both want a standard that can be applied consistently.

The difference is not who is more rigorous, but where the rigour points. ENTJ more often puts attention on whether the rule can be executed: who signs, which day it takes effect, who rechecks it. INTP more often puts attention on whether the rule can be recomputed: at which step the two accounts diverge, whether the edge cases are internally consistent.

### When the definition does not line up, two necessary pieces of work

A blocked definition usually lacks two things: an executable arrangement, and a recomputable definition. ENTJ more often sees the first as the gap — who decides this, which day the change takes effect, when the old version stops being used; INTP more often sees the second as the gap — at which step the two calculations diverge, which keyword means different things in two places. The first turns a disagreement into responsibility and dates; the second turns it into a proposition that can be tested.

This has nothing to do with who speaks first or who moves first. In the same meeting, ENTJ may spend the whole hour on definitions, and INTP may be pushed into fixing an effective date; the difference is which gap each more often treats as the one that must be closed first.

Each approach leaves a blind spot. Someone who only closes the arrangement may weld a wrong definition into the process, and changing it next time means going through approval again; someone who only closes the definition may check it thoroughly while nobody publishes a new version. The cost is not about preference but about who has the authority and who is waiting for this number.

Keep the counterexamples too: when INTP is made the owner of the definition, they may also lay out the signing order; when ENTJ meets a rule they cannot make sense of, they may also turn the meeting into a definition seminar. A position describes emphasis inside the model, not a fixed sequence of actions.

### Why the categories match and the attitudes reverse

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe. The category order is identical — Thinking, Intuition, Sensing, Feeling from first to fourth — and what changes is the attitude marked at each position: Te against Ti, Ni against Ne, Se against Si, Fi against Fe.

The derivation starts with the first two positions. E/I decides whether the dominant turns outward or inward, and J/P decides whether the outward step is judging or perceiving. ENTJ leans E and J: the dominant is an outward judging function, extraverted Thinking, Te; the auxiliary must be an inward perceiving function, taking Intuition, so introverted Intuition, Ni. INTP leans I and P: the dominant is inward, introverted Thinking, Ti; the outward step is perceiving, so the auxiliary is extraverted Intuition, Ne. The third and fourth positions are filled by the remaining two categories, Se and Fi, and Si and Fe.

Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not consistent across tables: some give only the function name, some label differently. This page uses the common writing and does not attribute that labelling to the Foundation as its only convention. Positions describe emphasis in preference and are not used to predict behavioural order, whether a collaboration goes smoothly, or mutual attraction. The four preferences are explained one by one in the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp).

sections.body_md:
Align three conditions before reading: the same version of the definition, the same batch of source documents, the same reporting deadline. Those conditions are what makes the two columns comparable; if one produces the numbers and the other only reviews, duty will cover both columns.

The six rows come from the same definition, the same data and the same signatory; the right-hand column states which axis the row sits on. The same person would switch columns under different conditions, so read the conditions before the tendency.

| The same event (one definition, one batch of documents, one deadline) | ENTJ: an example starting from execution conditions | INTP: an example starting from definitional consistency | Where this row's basis sits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A definition note arrives; can it be used as it stands | May prefer to agree on a provisional implementation plan under the same approval requirements | May prefer to keep several implementation options open while reviewing the same draft | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| The departments' figures differ substantially | Look for a pattern across affected reports that could explain the gap | Look for a shared assumption that could explain where the calculations diverge | Looking for patterns and possible explanations, the shared N |
| Someone wants an exception for one client | Would the same exception criteria apply consistently to other clients in the same circumstances? | Does the proposed exception contradict the rule, and can it be stated consistently? | Basis for judgement, the shared T |
| The report structure needs a new version | May agree on provisional release and retirement dates within the same constraints | May keep multiple transition plans open while the same dependencies are clarified | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Asked to produce a number today | Produce it on the current definition, and list the gaps as actions with names attached | Add an intermediate table that can be recomputed, and mark which rows are not yet usable | Delivery conventions and recomputable evidence; both check |
| Quarterly review | Whether every milestone was assessed against the same criteria | Whether each conclusion follows from the evidence and the same set of assumptions | Basis for judgement, the shared T |

The differences in the table are not a scale of ability. An INTP with years of cost accounting more often starts from signatures and effective dates, and an ENTJ taking over definition management for the first time may spend two days reading the field notes. The same person also changes approach with the information held, the authority granted and whether someone is already waiting for the number, so these rows cannot be used to classify.
sections.title: ENTJ and INTP in one minute

sections.body_md:
Joining the same data team, the handover usually splits into two artefacts: a definition sheet that states the signature and effective date, and a validation note that can be recomputed. Who writes which is decided by authority and familiarity, not by type.

### The quarterly management report: value shipped or value confirmed as delivered

(Fictional scene.) Three days before close, the sales team counts the value of orders shipped, the analysis team counts the value of orders confirmed as delivered, and the two internal totals differ substantially. This concerns the extraction basis of internal management reports only, not accounting revenue recognition; the external accounting basis is determined by finance under the applicable policy and contract terms, and this page compares extraction and review only, offering no accounting treatment advice.

One trade-off is about how this definition lands: bring the three parties together, agree a temporary method for the quarter, put it in writing by email, name an effective date, note when the old version stops, and turn the difference into a reconciliation sheet with an owner on every line.

The other trade-off is about whether the definition is consistent: go through the extraction conditions of both reports, find that the difference concentrates in the batch shipped across the month end, and that "signed" corresponds to two timestamps in the system, either of which can be justified.

The same analyst can do both kinds of check, and each trade-off has a cost. Someone watching only implementation may treat this quarter's temporary method as the conclusion and cover up the two-timestamp problem; someone watching only consistency may check thoroughly and miss the reporting window.

The check: each writes three lines — which field was used this time, which documents were affected, and where the problem should be stopped next time — then they swap and compare line by line. This is organising information, not scoring anyone.

### Explaining a definition change to the business: how to write the email

(Fictional scene.) The business lead will not accept the change, because the bonus is tied to the old number. One approach calculates the scope of impact and offers a transition period and a remedy; the other points out which orders the old definition necessarily gets wrong, with two specific order numbers attached. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

The sticking point is not the argument but the basis: an email with only a plan reads as pressure, and one with only flaws reads as evasion. Split it into two sections — what changes and when it takes effect, and why it cannot stay — and with both present the reader knows what to do.

Two counterexamples: ENTJ may leave the conclusion out for now so the other person can step back without losing face; INTP may accept a definition they are not happy with in order to hit the reporting deadline. Both show the same person changing basis under different conditions, and a single piece of writing is not a criterion.

### A fingerprint lock for the parents' flat

(Fictional scene.) Your parents keep misplacing their keys and have a fixed budget for a fingerprint lock. One approach weighs price, availability and support. Another checks the door thickness, the existing holes and whether there is a way to unlock the door during a power outage. Either person could do both. This fictional example illustrates buying criteria and cannot identify someone’s type.

Each focus has its own failure mode: buying on budget and schedule may end with a door that is the wrong thickness; checking only specifications may take so long that the parents are still dealing with misplaced keys. Both are guarding against the same thing — buying wrong and returning — one with time and budget, the other with a specification sheet.

Keep the counterexamples: INTP may also order immediately when the parents push; ENTJ may also have someone measure the door before ordering. Who pays, who lives nearby and who arranges the installation all change where the attention lands.

The parents will not care which line of thinking is cleverer; they will ask which day it can be fitted. The check: before ordering, each writes three conditions that would force a return — door thickness, hole spacing, unlocking when the power is out — and only pay when all three match, asking the seller first if one does not.
sections.title: ENTJ and INTP at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
The first slip is treating volume in a meeting as evidence of type. ENTJ will also listen through a round before speaking on an unfamiliar topic; INTP can also go into great detail on a field they have checked themselves. How much someone speaks depends on familiarity with the topic, how the meeting is chaired and where they sit, and cannot be read backwards into a type.

The second is treating rigour as the common trait of Thinking types. Both lean T, and T is not the differing item in this pair; the fork is E/I and J/P — whether attention goes outward or inward more often, and whether the outward step forms an arrangement or keeps options. Whether closure happens in the meeting or afterwards depends on the chair, the agenda and who has authority, and is not a type clue.

The third is treating the last signatory as the more senior. Signing is a role the process assigns; ENTJ only offers comments on modules someone else owns, and INTP signs when made responsible. Material that only records "who decided" distinguishes jobs.

The fourth is treating "who moves first" as the criterion. On the same definition, whether responsibility or the definition gets dismantled first depends heavily on deadlines, authority and information held; recording the order as type evidence collapses the moment someone changes role or project.
sections.title: ENTJ and INTP: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
When two results differ, check the item bank first: the same questionnaire, language version, time window and scoring convention. Then look at the answering situation — if you were mainly thinking about the demands of your job, the answers may reflect a role rather than an everyday preference, and you cannot infer from that which way the score would move.

An exercise you can run yourself: take one fictional definition note and write two sets of conditions. First: a clear signatory exists but the field definitions are undecided — what is still needed. Second: the field definitions are settled but nobody has the authority to publish — what is still needed. In each, write down how authority, deadline and missing information change your choice.

These notes are for understanding trade-offs; they are not scored, do not assign a type, and set no minimum number. Counterexamples matter as much: using the other kind of basis on the same sort of matter shows both approaches are within your range.
sections.title: ENTJ and INTP: how to keep observing

items.answer:
They can disagree about either. In type dynamics, they share N and T and differ in where the dominant process is directed (E/I) and which kind of process faces outward (J/P).

In the fictional reporting example, one question is how to put the rule into effect. Another is whether two people applying it would get the same number. Either type can ask both, and the order does not identify ENTJ or INTP.
items.question: Are ENTJ and INTP arguing about the conclusion or about the method?

items.answer:
Under the notation used here, what changes is whether each function is directed inward or outward. In Te–Ni–Se–Fi and Ti–Ne–Si–Fe, the first to fourth positions are Thinking, Intuition, Sensing and Feeling in both, and only the attitude marked at each position is opposite.

The derivation needs only the first two positions: E/I decides whether the dominant turns outward or inward, and J/P decides whether the outward step is judging or perceiving. ENTJ leans E and J, so the dominant is extraverted Thinking Te and the auxiliary introverted Intuition Ni; INTP leans I and P, so the dominant is introverted Thinking Ti and the auxiliary extraverted Intuition Ne. The attitude of the third process is disputed across sources, so confirm the source with a differing version and then read the first two. Positions describe emphasis only and predict neither behavioural order nor whether two people work well together.
items.question: They differ by only two letters — why do the four categories match while the attitudes reverse?

items.answer:
Yes, but not by one instance of settling or polishing, and not by trigger conditions such as being cornered.

What discriminates better is the reason: across a comparable situation, do you more often cite "who signs this rule, which day it takes effect, who to ask when it does not apply", or "at which step this definition diverges, whether the edge cases are consistent"? Both types settle and both polish; being pushed by authority, deadline or duty reflects the conditions of the moment. Single behaviour is not a criterion, and the same person's trade-off changes with the role or project.
items.question: INTP also settles a definition, and ENTJ also polishes one — can they still be told apart?

items.answer:
Both types can do it; this section does not judge competence, only how to divide the work.

Divide by authority, business knowledge and data permission: whoever can confirm the effective arrangement writes the signature and the dates, whoever can recompute writes the applicable boundary and the exclusions, and each reviews the other. If one person holds both, both documents get written and a third person reviews. An exercise: take a fictional definition note and write two versions, "three lines of effective arrangement" and "three definition boundaries", then swap and fill each other's gaps.
items.question: Who is better suited to own a reporting definition?

items.answer:
Most often at "the meeting ended without an effective date" and "the effective date is set but the definition is not aligned".

A usable agreement: every definition change leaves two things — who signs and which day it takes effect, and one sentence on when the rule does not apply. The signature and date are written by whoever can confirm them, the applicable boundary by whoever can recompute, and missing either means it does not pass; who writes which part follows authority and familiarity, not type.
items.question: Where do ENTJ and INTP most often get stuck in a data team?

items.answer:
Treat both as clues only: check the assessment name, version, language and scoring convention, then which kind of experience you referred to — what you do when you have a choice, or what work requires you to do.

If the same tool gives interpretable dimension scores and a boundary, look at whether E/I and J/P sit near it; sitting near a boundary only means that label is sensitive to changes in your answers, not that two complete types both hold. If there are only type labels and no dimension scores or scoring notes, do not back-calculate a gap, and do not infer that you are on a boundary.
items.question: I test as ENTJ and also as INTP — how should I use both results?

sections.body_md:
The preference definitions follow the [official Myers-Briggs facts page](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts); the type dynamics framework follows the [Foundation's account of type dynamics processes](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and the [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

The arrangement of the four positions on this page, especially the attitude of the third process, is the common four-function notation adopted here and is an editorial convention; sources handle it differently, and this writing is not presented as the Foundation's only version.

The quarterly management report, the definition-change email and the lock replacement are editorial composites, written only to practise discrimination, corresponding to no real person or event, and not evidence of behavioural frequency. The internal management reports discussed here cover extraction and review only and constitute no accounting, audit or compliance opinion; the external definition and accounting recognition are determined by finance under the applicable policy and authority.

Assessment results are not for ranking ability, screening candidates or predicting relationships.

The FermatMind assessment uses its own item bank and scoring; the scope is set out in the [scoring and evidence note](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
